pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, liquidity is adequate. Caesars Entertainment, Inc. held USD 864 million of unrestricted cash and USD 2,083 million of revolver availability on the company basis at September 30, 2026, together USD 2,947 million, and the CEI revolver was undrawn after USD 160 million was drawn at December 31, 2025 [CP-1]. No notes mature before 2029. Debt falling due is USD 28 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 114 million in 2027 and USD 646 million in 2028, which is mostly the CEI Term Loan A of USD 609 million; the CEI revolver and that term loan both mature on January 31, 2028. Nothing matures within twelve months of the as-of date beyond scheduled amortisation, so the 2028 date becomes a current-year issue from early 2027 (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

Second, the lease structure is the main fixed claim. Long-term financing obligations to VICI and GLPI of USD 13,188 million sit outside the USD 11,659 million of debt, and the lease payment schedule at December 31, 2025 shows USD 1,392 million in 2027, USD 1,424 million in 2028 and USD 1,446 million in 2029 [CP-1; annual report]. Lease cash interest of about USD 1,371 million over the last twelve months compares with USD 741 million of cash interest on debt. Adjusted EBITDA excludes this rent, so total debt plus financing obligations over Adjusted EBITDA is 6.95x against 3.26x for debt alone, and Adjusted EBITDA over all cash interest is 1.69x. Adjusted EBITDA less purchases of property and equipment of USD 664 million gives USD 2,909 million against USD 2,112 million of cash interest, or 1.38x (calculated). Net loss attributable to Caesars was USD 533 million over the last twelve months.

Third, leverage is flat to slightly better on debt and slightly worse once leases are counted. Debt-only leverage moved from 3.29x at FY2025 to 3.26x at Q3 2026 as debt fell by USD 246 million, while the lease-inclusive ratio moved from 6.90x to 6.95x because the financing obligation grew by USD 92 million and last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 3,624 million to USD 3,573 million [CP-1]. The company explains that in the early years of these leases cash payments are below the interest expense recognised, so the obligation increases.

Fourth, earnings are mixed by segment. Las Vegas Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,179 million for nine months 2026 against USD 1,281 million, attributed by the company to fewer city-wide convention events and lower leisure visitation, while Regional rose to USD 1,447 million from USD 1,385 million, helped by the Caesars Windsor consolidation from March 3, 2026, and Caesars Digital rose to USD 181 million from USD 151 million [CP-1; CP-1A]. Las Vegas carries the highest segment margin, so its softness weighs more than its revenue share of 35.3% suggests (Analyst Interpretation).

Fifth, refinancing risk is concentrated. Maturities of USD 1,574 million in 2029 and USD 3,962 million in 2030 together are USD 5,536 million, 47.5% of face debt of USD 11,659 million, and variable-rate borrowings of USD 5.8 billion are about half of debt with no derivatives held [CP-1]. A move of 1.00% in the base rate would change annual cash interest on that variable debt by about USD 58 million (calculated, before any floors), against USD 741 million of cash interest on debt over the last twelve months.

Sixth, the pending acquisition is the largest open item. The agreement was signed on May 27, 2026 at USD 31.00 per share in cash, stockholders approved it on September 22, 2026, and closing needs antitrust and gaming approvals, with an initial end date of May 27, 2027, extendable to November 27, 2027 [CP-1A]. A USD 200 million fee is payable by the company in specified circumstances and a USD 450 million fee by the buyer in others. The sources do not describe merger financing, the equity contribution, rollover terms or the treatment of the CEI Credit Agreement, the notes or the Caesars Virginia facilities at closing. That is a missing datapoint, not an adverse finding (Insufficient Information).

Seventh, covenant headroom cannot be measured. The CEI revolver and Term Loan A carry a maximum net total leverage ratio of 6.50:1 and a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of 2.0:1, the Caesars Virginia facilities 4:1 and 1.05:1, and the GLPI Leases a minimum adjusted revenue to rent ratio of 1.20:1, with compliance stated at September 30, 2026 but no ratio values printed. The ratios computed here are not covenant ratios and must not be compared with those levels (Insufficient Information).

runs.text: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and no near-term maturity wall: USD 2,947 million of liquidity against USD 142 million of scheduled principal through 2027, with the revolver undrawn (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (2) Diversified footprint and a growing digital segment: 54 properties in 20 jurisdictions, Regional at 50.1% and Las Vegas at 35.3% of FY2025 net revenues, and Caesars Digital Adjusted EBITDA up to USD 181 million for nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (3) Conservative capital return and debt direction: no cash dividends, no share repurchases in nine months 2026, debt down USD 246 million since FY2025 and asset sale proceeds applied to redeeming the 2027 notes (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (4) Moderate debt-only leverage of 3.26x and debt-only cash interest cover of 4.82x (Analyst Interpretation on company Adjusted EBITDA; CP-1). (5) Stockholder approval of the merger removes one execution uncertainty (Documentary Fact; CP-1A).

Weaknesses. (1) Fixed lease claims outside debt: USD 13,188 million of financing obligations and about USD 1,371 million a year of rent cash interest, leaving all-in cover of 1.69x and lease-inclusive leverage of 6.95x (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (2) Earnings drift and net losses: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,672 million against USD 2,723 million and a net loss attributable to Caesars of USD 283 million for nine months 2026, with the Las Vegas segment, which has the highest margin, declining (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (3) Refinancing concentration in 2029 and 2030 of USD 5,536 million and about half of debt at floating rates (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (4) Opaque post-closing structure: merger financing and debt treatment undisclosed, and the buyer named differently in the filings and the releases (Insufficient Information; CP-1A). (5) Covenant and agreement evidence missing: levels printed without ratio values, definitions or executed documents (Insufficient Information; CP-0, CP-1). (6) The Adjusted EBITDA add-backs, including transaction costs and other of USD 64 million for nine months 2026, are management defined, and the company says its definition may differ from those in its debt and lease agreements (Management Language; CP-1).

runs.text: The transaction is a pending cash acquisition of Caesars Entertainment, Inc. On May 27, 2026 the company, Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC, Empire Merger Sub, Inc., Landry's Fertitta, LLC (for Section 9.14 of the agreement only) and Hospitality Headquarters, Inc. (for Section 9.14(j) only) signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger under which Merger Sub merges into the company and the company survives as a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Fertitta Gaming (Q3 10-Q page:6). The earnings releases state that the agreement is with Fertitta Entertainment, Inc. and that it was announced on May 28, 2026 (Q3 release page:4). The two names are logged below as an unresolved conflict. Each share other than excluded, parent rollover and dissenting shares converts into $31.00 in cash plus, if closing has not occurred by June 26, 2027, a ticking fee of $0.007150 per day from the first day of the following month; parent rollover shares convert into shares of the surviving corporation, and the sources do not disclose a rollover percentage (Q3 10-Q page:7). Restricted stock units are cancelled for cash at the same consideration (Q3 10-Q page:7).

The status is stockholder-approved and awaiting regulatory conditions. The company filed its proxy statement on August 26, 2026 and the proposals were approved at a special meeting on September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:7). Closing remains conditioned on expiry or termination of the HSR Act waiting period and receipt of certain gaming regulatory approvals; the filings do not say which approvals have been received (Q3 10-Q page:8 and page:62). The initial end date is May 27, 2027, extended automatically to August 27, 2027 and then November 27, 2027 if only those regulatory conditions remain open (Q3 10-Q page:8). A termination fee of $200 million is payable by the company in specified circumstances and a reverse termination fee of $450 million by Fertitta Gaming in others, including antitrust or gaming law prohibitions or the end date occurring with only regulatory conditions open (Q3 10-Q page:9). A no-shop has applied since July 11, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:8). On completion the common stock is delisted from NASDAQ and deregistered, which ends the public filings that this credit view relies on (Q3 10-Q page:10).

For debt, the sources give no use of proceeds, sources and uses, new debt raised, financing commitments, equity contribution or liquidity effect. The filings list risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction and the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all among forward-looking risks (Q3 10-Q page:57), and the company represented its present debt financing and covenants in the agreement (Q3 10-Q page:8). They do not state whether the existing CEI Credit Agreement, the CEI notes or the CVA facilities are repaid, assumed, amended or subject to a change-of-control offer at closing. That absence is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion. The company incurred transaction costs related to the merger of 10 for Q2 2026 and 12 for Q3 2026, 22 for nine months 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:9; Q3 10-Q page:10).

New debt issues: none appear in the nine months to September 30, 2026. The debt table lists no instrument issued in 2026, and proceeds from long-term debt and revolving credit facilities of 1,335 against repayments of 1,581 reflect revolver activity and scheduled repayment (Q3 10-Q page:5). The last term debt issues in the filings are the CEI Senior Notes due 2032 of $1.1 billion at 6.00% on October 17, 2024, the CEI Senior Secured Notes due 2032 of $1.5 billion at 6.50% and the CEI Term Loan B-1 of $2.9 billion on February 6, 2024, and the Caesars Virginia facilities of April 26, 2024 (Q3 10-Q page:18 to page:20). The CEI Senior Notes due 2027 of $546 million were redeemed on July 8, 2025 with revolver borrowings and note proceeds (10-K page:80). Merger-related debt is not described.

fields.value: - Debt issuers: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. (CEI) is the borrower under the CEI Credit Agreement and the issuer of the CEI notes (Q3 10-Q page:17 and page:19 to page:20). CEI debt is guaranteed by `each existing and future material wholly owned domestic subsidiary` (page:21). The guarantor names and the restricted-group definition are not in the supplied text.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Separate borrower group: Caesars Virginia, LLC is the borrower under the CVA facilities, which are secured by its assets; `CEI does not provide a guarantee of these facilities.` (Q3 10-Q page:21). CEI holds a `50.0% variable interest` in CVA Holdco, LLC and consolidates it as primary beneficiary, with a minority interest (page:29). Consolidated debt therefore includes debt that is not guaranteed by the parent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lease counterparties: VICI Properties L.P. (the VICI Leases) and GLP Capital, L.P. (the GLPI Leases) (Q3 10-Q page:36). The leases are accounted for as failed sale-leasebacks and appear in `Long-term financing obligations`, separate from `Long-term debt` on the balance sheet (page:2).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquirer: the Merger Agreement parties are Caesars, Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC and Empire Merger Sub, Inc. (Q3 10-Q page:6). The earnings releases instead name `Fertitta Entertainment, Inc.` as the company that will acquire Caesars (Q3 release page:4). The 10-Q heading also reads `Proposed Merger of Caesars Entertainment, Inc. with Fertitta Entertainment, Inc.` The relationship between Fertitta Entertainment, Inc. and Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC is not explained in the supplied text. It is an unresolved identity distinction, carried as a gap.

fields.value: - Usable coverage: one audited annual report, three unaudited interim reports and three releases cover FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026 with prior-year comparatives. Together they support a financial foundation, a debt and lease map, and the merger narrative up to October 27, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strongest contrary evidence: the pending acquisition can change ownership and leverage. The Q3 10-Q lists `risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction` (page:57) and `the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all`. The supplied text does not say how the existing CEI debt or the CVA facilities are treated at closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Source risk mechanism: lease payments to VICI and GLPI run through `Long-term financing obligations` and interest expense, not through the debt table, and Adjusted EBITDA `excludes the expense associated with certain of our leases` (Q3 release page:3). A consumer reading only total debt or Adjusted EBITDA would understate fixed claims and overstate coverage. Consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 must carry the lease obligations and the lease cash interest alongside debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Second mechanism: the covenant definitions govern headroom, and the company states that its Adjusted EBITDA definition `may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt or lease agreements` (Q3 10-Q page:49). Consequence: CP-2 can report printed levels and the compliance statement but cannot verify headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The reported base supports a debt-only view and a lease-inclusive view, and the two give very different pictures. On the company's own measures, debt is 11,659 at Q3 2026 (face value), net debt is 10,795, and last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is 3,573, giving 3.26x and 3.02x. But Adjusted EBITDA is stated before the rent on the VICI and GLPI leases, which the company accounts for as financing obligations of 13,188 outside debt. Adding those obligations lifts leverage to 6.95x, and adding the roughly 1,371 of rent cash interest to the 741 of cash interest on debt gives cash interest cover of 1.69x. Both views use the same company Adjusted EBITDA, so neither is a covenant ratio. Earnings are drifting lower (Adjusted EBITDA 2,672 for 9M 2026 against 2,723 for 9M 2025, with Las Vegas down and Regional and Digital up) and net loss attributable to Caesars widened to (283) from (252). Liquidity is adequate in the near term and nothing in the debt table matures before 2028 beyond amortisation. The pending acquisition adds uncertainty about the debt, but the supplied sources do not say how existing debt is treated.

The 10-K splits them at December 31, 2025 as GLPI Leases 1,284 and VICI Leases 11,705 (10-K page:117), which total 12,989; the remaining 107 of the 13,096 balance is not itemised in the text read. fields.value: The credit story is a large, lease-heavy casino operator with a diversified but physically concentrated revenue base, entering a change of control on terms the sources describe only in part. Regional properties and Las Vegas supply about 85% of net revenues, Caesars Digital is the growing third leg, and the VICI and GLPI real estate leases make the company a tenant at 25 of the 47 casinos it owns or leases. Ownership today is public, with about 273 holders of record, no sponsor named in the context and no dividend history. The pending merger converts each share into cash of $31.00 plus a ticking fee after June 26, 2027, was approved by stockholders on September 22, 2026, and remains subject to antitrust and gaming approvals with an outside date that can run to November 27, 2027. For creditors, the open questions are who finances the purchase, whether the existing notes and loans stay in place, and whether leverage rises; the sources state that financing risk exists but give no terms. Until the Merger Agreement, proxy statement and financing papers are supplied, the transaction can be described but not assessed for debt effects.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction is a pending cash acquisition of Caesars Entertainment, Inc. On May 27, 2026 the company, Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC, Empire Merger Sub, Inc., Landry's Fertitta, LLC (for Section 9.14 of the agreement only) and Hospitality Headquarters, Inc. (for Section 9.14(j) only) signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger under which Merger Sub merges into the company and the company survives as a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Fertitta Gaming (Q3 10-Q page:6). The earnings releases state that the agreement is with `Fertitta Entertainment, Inc.` and that it was announced on May 28, 2026 (Q3 release page:4). The two names are logged below as an unresolved conflict. Each share other than excluded, parent rollover and dissenting shares converts into $31.00 in cash plus, if closing has not occurred by June 26, 2027, a ticking fee of $0.007150 per day from the first day of the following month; parent rollover shares convert into shares of the surviving corporation, and the sources do not disclose a rollover percentage (Q3 10-Q page:7). Restricted stock units are cancelled for cash at the same consideration (Q3 10-Q page:7).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The status is stockholder-approved and awaiting regulatory conditions. The company filed its proxy statement on August 26, 2026 and the proposals were approved at a special meeting on September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:7). Closing remains conditioned on expiry or termination of the HSR Act waiting period and receipt of certain gaming regulatory approvals; the filings do not say which approvals have been received (Q3 10-Q page:8 and page:62). The initial end date is May 27, 2027, extended automatically to August 27, 2027 and then November 27, 2027 if only those regulatory conditions remain open (Q3 10-Q page:8). A termination fee of $200 million is payable by the company in specified circumstances and a reverse termination fee of $450 million by Fertitta Gaming in others, including antitrust or gaming law prohibitions or the end date occurring with only regulatory conditions open (Q3 10-Q page:9). A no-shop has applied since July 11, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:8). On completion the common stock is delisted from NASDAQ and deregistered, which ends the public filings that this credit view relies on (Q3 10-Q page:10).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For debt, the sources give no use of proceeds, sources and uses, new debt raised, financing commitments, equity contribution or liquidity effect. The filings list `risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction` and `the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all` among forward-looking risks (Q3 10-Q page:57), and the company represented its `present debt financing and covenants` in the agreement (Q3 10-Q page:8). They do not state whether the existing CEI Credit Agreement, the CEI notes or the CVA facilities are repaid, assumed, amended or subject to a change-of-control offer at closing. That absence is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion. The company incurred transaction costs related to the merger of 10 for Q2 2026 and 12 for Q3 2026, 22 for nine months 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:9; Q3 10-Q page:10).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues: none appear in the nine months to September 30, 2026. The debt table lists no instrument issued in 2026, and proceeds from long-term debt and revolving credit facilities of 1,335 against repayments of 1,581 reflect revolver activity and scheduled repayment (Q3 10-Q page:5). The last term debt issues in the filings are the CEI Senior Notes due 2032 of $1.1 billion at 6.00% on October 17, 2024, the CEI Senior Secured Notes due 2032 of $1.5 billion at 6.50% and the CEI Term Loan B-1 of $2.9 billion on February 6, 2024, and the Caesars Virginia facilities of April 26, 2024 (Q3 10-Q page:18 to page:20). The CEI Senior Notes due 2027 of $546 million were redeemed on July 8, 2025 with revolver borrowings and note proceeds (10-K page:80). Merger-related debt is not described.

fields.value: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. (issuer id `czr`), as of 2026-11-05, pathway `credit_snapshot`, asks for the fundamental credit view from the upstream financial base and the business and transaction context. Scope is the consolidated company in USD millions for FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, with no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Locators in tables are `page:N` of the pinned `.jsonl` text, not printed page numbers. Consistency with upstream: this answer agrees with CP-0, CP-1 and CP-1A. It adds the lease payment schedule from the annual report and a few new calculations, all shown below; it corrects no earlier handoff.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. is a liquid but lease-burdened credit: debt-only leverage of 3.26x looks moderate, yet fixed-charge cover is thin and the change of control leaves the debt outlook open. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 2,947 million, an undrawn revolver and a first notes maturity only in 2029. The weakest point is fixed charges: USD 13,188 million of lease financing obligations sit outside debt, lifting leverage to 6.95x and holding cash interest cover to 1.69x while Adjusted EBITDA slipped to USD 2,672 million for nine months 2026. What decides the outcome is how the pending acquisition is financed and whether the existing notes and loans stay in place, which the supplied sources do not say.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, liquidity is adequate. Caesars Entertainment, Inc. held USD 864 million of unrestricted cash and USD 2,083 million of revolver availability on the company basis at September 30, 2026, together USD 2,947 million, and the CEI revolver was undrawn after USD 160 million was drawn at December 31, 2025 [CP-1]. No notes mature before 2029. Debt falling due is USD 28 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 114 million in 2027 and USD 646 million in 2028, which is mostly the CEI Term Loan A of USD 609 million; the CEI revolver and that term loan both mature on January 31, 2028. Nothing matures within twelve months of the as-of date beyond scheduled amortisation, so the 2028 date becomes a current-year issue from early 2027 (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, the lease structure is the main fixed claim. Long-term financing obligations to VICI and GLPI of USD 13,188 million sit outside the USD 11,659 million of debt, and the lease payment schedule at December 31, 2025 shows USD 1,392 million in 2027, USD 1,424 million in 2028 and USD 1,446 million in 2029 [CP-1; annual report]. Lease cash interest of about USD 1,371 million over the last twelve months compares with USD 741 million of cash interest on debt. Adjusted EBITDA excludes this rent, so total debt plus financing obligations over Adjusted EBITDA is 6.95x against 3.26x for debt alone, and Adjusted EBITDA over all cash interest is 1.69x. Adjusted EBITDA less purchases of property and equipment of USD 664 million gives USD 2,909 million against USD 2,112 million of cash interest, or 1.38x (calculated). Net loss attributable to Caesars was USD 533 million over the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, leverage is flat to slightly better on debt and slightly worse once leases are counted. Debt-only leverage moved from 3.29x at FY2025 to 3.26x at Q3 2026 as debt fell by USD 246 million, while the lease-inclusive ratio moved from 6.90x to 6.95x because the financing obligation grew by USD 92 million and last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 3,624 million to USD 3,573 million [CP-1]. The company explains that in the early years of these leases cash payments are below the interest expense recognised, so the obligation increases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, earnings are mixed by segment. Las Vegas Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,179 million for nine months 2026 against USD 1,281 million, attributed by the company to fewer city-wide convention events and lower leisure visitation, while Regional rose to USD 1,447 million from USD 1,385 million, helped by the Caesars Windsor consolidation from March 3, 2026, and Caesars Digital rose to USD 181 million from USD 151 million [CP-1; CP-1A]. Las Vegas carries the highest segment margin, so its softness weighs more than its revenue share of 35.3% suggests (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, refinancing risk is concentrated. Maturities of USD 1,574 million in 2029 and USD 3,962 million in 2030 together are USD 5,536 million, 47.5% of face debt of USD 11,659 million, and variable-rate borrowings of USD 5.8 billion are about half of debt with no derivatives held [CP-1]. A move of 1.00% in the base rate would change annual cash interest on that variable debt by about USD 58 million (calculated, before any floors), against USD 741 million of cash interest on debt over the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, the pending acquisition is the largest open item. The agreement was signed on May 27, 2026 at USD 31.00 per share in cash, stockholders approved it on September 22, 2026, and closing needs antitrust and gaming approvals, with an initial end date of May 27, 2027, extendable to November 27, 2027 [CP-1A]. A USD 200 million fee is payable by the company in specified circumstances and a USD 450 million fee by the buyer in others. The sources do not describe merger financing, the equity contribution, rollover terms or the treatment of the CEI Credit Agreement, the notes or the Caesars Virginia facilities at closing. That is a missing datapoint, not an adverse finding (Insufficient Information).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seventh, covenant headroom cannot be measured. The CEI revolver and Term Loan A carry a maximum net total leverage ratio of 6.50:1 and a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of 2.0:1, the Caesars Virginia facilities 4:1 and 1.05:1, and the GLPI Leases a minimum adjusted revenue to rent ratio of 1.20:1, with compliance stated at September 30, 2026 but no ratio values printed. The ratios computed here are not covenant ratios and must not be compared with those levels (Insufficient Information).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and no near-term maturity wall: USD 2,947 million of liquidity against USD 142 million of scheduled principal through 2027, with the revolver undrawn (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (2) Diversified footprint and a growing digital segment: 54 properties in 20 jurisdictions, Regional at 50.1% and Las Vegas at 35.3% of FY2025 net revenues, and Caesars Digital Adjusted EBITDA up to USD 181 million for nine months 2026 (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (3) Conservative capital return and debt direction: no cash dividends, no share repurchases in nine months 2026, debt down USD 246 million since FY2025 and asset sale proceeds applied to redeeming the 2027 notes (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (4) Moderate debt-only leverage of 3.26x and debt-only cash interest cover of 4.82x (Analyst Interpretation on company Adjusted EBITDA; CP-1). (5) Stockholder approval of the merger removes one execution uncertainty (Documentary Fact; CP-1A).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. (1) Fixed lease claims outside debt: USD 13,188 million of financing obligations and about USD 1,371 million a year of rent cash interest, leaving all-in cover of 1.69x and lease-inclusive leverage of 6.95x (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (2) Earnings drift and net losses: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,672 million against USD 2,723 million and a net loss attributable to Caesars of USD 283 million for nine months 2026, with the Las Vegas segment, which has the highest margin, declining (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (3) Refinancing concentration in 2029 and 2030 of USD 5,536 million and about half of debt at floating rates (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (4) Opaque post-closing structure: merger financing and debt treatment undisclosed, and the buyer named differently in the filings and the releases (Insufficient Information; CP-1A). (5) Covenant and agreement evidence missing: levels printed without ratio values, definitions or executed documents (Insufficient Information; CP-0, CP-1). (6) The Adjusted EBITDA add-backs, including transaction costs and other of USD 64 million for nine months 2026, are management defined, and the company says its definition may differ from those in its debt and lease agreements (Management Language; CP-1).
